meta-title: MFP — Music For Programming player for your terminal
meta-description: MFP is a free, open-source terminal player for musicforprogramming.net: live audio visualizer, color themes and media keys. Written in Rust for Linux and macOS.
meta-og-title: MFP — Music For Programming, in your terminal
meta-og-description: A free, open-source terminal player for musicforprogramming.net with a live visualizer, color themes and media keys. Written in Rust.
meta-twitter-title: MFP — Music For Programming, in your terminal
meta-twitter-description: A free, open-source terminal player for musicforprogramming.net with a live visualizer, color themes and media keys.
meta-image-alt: MFP: Music For Programming, in your terminal. A terminal window showing the episode list, the player and an audio visualizer with colored bars.
hero-lead: Lightweight terminal player for musicforprogramming.net. Streams directly, no external dependencies, MPRIS support.
demo-aria-label: Interactive mock of the mfp terminal player. An episode list is on the left; the player with title, progress bar, volume, shuffle state and MPRIS dot is on the right, with an animated audio visualizer below it. Click it and press v to change the visualizer style, V to turn it off, h to hide the list, p to pause. Sample episodes only.
demo-hint-live: keys on: v V h p n b s f m + - j k
demo-note: A small mock with sample episodes and a made-up spectrum, drawn the way the real player draws its screen. The last two themes are custom theme files, to show what you can make. More about themes.
features-starts-playing-after-a: Starts playing after a 512 KB buffer — no waiting for the full episode to download.
features-six-animated-styles-that: Six animated styles that move with the music. Switch with v, turn off with V. See the styles.
features-aria-sketch-of-a-filled: Sketch of a filled hill shape that follows the sound
features-a-full-screen-player: A full-screen player with an episode list and search; play/pause, volume, mute, next, previous, shuffle — all from the keyboard while it runs.
features-six-built-in-themes: Six built-in themes, or make your own with a small text file. Choose your colors.
features-exposes-d-bus-mpris: Exposes D-Bus MPRIS so Polybar, KDE, GNOME, and any media client can see and control it.
features-save-episodes-to-config: Save episodes to ~/.config/mfp/downloads/ with d or mfp download. mfp still streams episodes when you play them.
features-mark-episodes-as-favorites: Mark episodes as favorites and play only those, with or without shuffle.
features-pure-rust-audio-pipeline: Pure Rust audio pipeline — no mpv, no ffmpeg. MP3, FLAC, AAC, ALAC, Vorbis, WAV.
install-requires-rust-stable-the: Requires Rust stable. The release profile strips debug info and optimizes for size (the binary is about 5 MB).
install-copy-the-binary-system: Copy the binary system-wide so you can run mfp from anywhere.
install-running-mfp-opens-the: Running mfp opens the full-screen player. It is the same as mfp play. Press q to quit. See Using the player for all the keys.
usage-text-mode-type-a: # text mode, type a command + Enter
usage-running-mfp-with-no: Running mfp with no command is the same as mfp play and accepts the same options.
usage-aria-table-of-play-options: Table of play options, scrolls sideways on small screens
usage-start-at-this-episode: Start at this episode number (for example 75). It starts at the first episode titled “Episode N…”; a plain text match, so 1 also matches “Episode 12”. If nothing matches, it starts at the beginning.
usage-shuffle-the-playlist-toggle: Shuffle the playlist. Toggle it at any time with s.
usage-use-the-plain-text: Use the plain text mode instead of the full-screen player. More about text mode.
usage-start-with-the-episode: Start with the episode list hidden (player only). It cannot be combined with --plain.
player-title: What you see and what to press
player-when-you-run-mfp: When you run mfp it fills your terminal window. On a normal-sized window you get two panels side by side:
player-episodes-left-the-full: Episodes (left). The full list of episodes. A ▶ marks the one that is playing and a ★ marks your favorites.
player-player-right-the-episode: Player (right). The episode title, a progress bar with the time played and the total time, the volume, whether shuffle is on, and a dot that is filled when your desktop media keys are connected. Below that you see the visualizer and a line for short messages, such as "downloading" or an error.
player-help-line-bottom-a: Help line (bottom). A reminder of the most useful keys.
player-press-h-to-hide: Press h to hide the episode list and give the whole window to the player and visualizer. Press h again to bring the list back. You can also start with the list hidden using mfp play --compact.
player-you-do-not-have: You do not have to choose: until you press h, mfp picks the view from the size of your window. Below about 80 columns by 16 rows it uses the compact view by itself and switches back when you make the window bigger. Once you press h, your choice sticks for the rest of the session. Showing the list needs at least 64 by 12; on a smaller window h does nothing. If the window is really tiny (under 40 by 9) mfp asks you to make it bigger. When the list is hidden, the keys that move around the list do nothing.
player-just-press-the-key: Just press the key, no Enter needed. Keys are case-sensitive: v and V do different things.
player-move-a-page-at: Move a page at a time
player-press-and-start-typing: Press / and start typing: the list narrows down as you type. While you are typing, letters go into the search box, so they will not trigger the keys above. Press Enter to keep the filtered list, or Esc to clear the search. The arrows, Page Up/Page Down, Home and End still move the selection while you search, and Ctrl+C always quits.
player-the-list-keys-moving: The list keys (moving, Enter, /) only work while the episode list is shown.
visualizer-while-an-episode-plays: While an episode plays, mfp draws the sound as a live animation under the player. It reacts to what you are hearing: bass on the left, treble on the right. When you pause, it settles down to nothing. It only listens; it never changes the audio.
visualizer-press-v-to-switch: Press v to switch to the next style, and V to turn the animation off or on. If it is off, v turns it on again with the next style. In the compact view the visualizer is shown when the window is at least 13 rows tall.
visualizer-classic-vertical-bars-this: Classic vertical bars. This is the default.
visualizer-aria-sketch-of-vertical-bars: Sketch of vertical bars of different heights
visualizer-bars-that-grow-up: Bars that grow up and down from a middle line.
visualizer-aria-sketch-of-bars-mirrored: Sketch of bars mirrored above and below a center line
visualizer-a-wavy-line-like: A wavy line, like an oscilloscope, drawn with tiny dots.
visualizer-columns-of-dots-with: Columns of dots with a small marker that lingers at the highest point.
visualizer-aria-sketch-of-columns-of: Sketch of columns of dots with markers on top
visualizer-a-smooth-filled-shape: A smooth filled shape that follows the sound.
visualizer-aria-sketch-of-a-filled: Sketch of a filled hill shape
visualizer-two-level-meters-one: Two level meters, one for the left speaker and one for the right.
visualizer-aria-sketch-of-two-horizontal: Sketch of two horizontal level meters, L and R
visualizer-these-sketches-are-only: These sketches are only an idea of the shape. The real thing is colored and moves; the colors come from your theme.
visualizer-the-style-you-pick: The style you pick with v and V lasts until you quit. To choose what mfp starts with, add a [visualizer] section to your config file:
visualizer-if-the-style-name: If the style name is not recognized, mfp starts with bars and writes a note to its log file.
themes-title: Make it look the way you like
themes-mfp-comes-with-six: mfp comes with six color themes. You choose one in the config file; there is deliberately no key to change the theme while listening, so a stray key press never repaints your screen.
themes-the-original-look-uses: The original look. Uses your terminal's own colors with a blue highlight, so it fits both dark and light terminals. This is what you get if you choose nothing.
themes-calm-blue-green-tones: Calm blue-green tones on a dark teal background.
themes-plain-black-and-white: Plain black and white with bright colors, easy to read on any screen. Uses your terminal's own basic colors (its black, white, bright cyan and so on), so the exact shades depend on your terminal.
themes-warm-earthy-colors-with: Warm, earthy colors with a yellow highlight.
themes-dark-purple-background-with: Dark purple background with pink and cyan accents.
themes-the-last-two-chips: The last two chips in the demo are not built in: they are theme files, like the ones in “Make your own theme” below, with every color set. Open one to see the whole file.
themes-soot-black-onyx-with: Soot-black onyx with aged gold and sage greens.
themes-deep-violet-night-with: Deep violet night with neon magenta, cyan and yellow.
themes-create-the-file-config: Create the file ~/.config/mfp/config.toml (create the folder if it does not exist yet) with the name of the theme:
themes-every-line-is-optional: Every line is optional. Leave out anything you do not want to change. Restart mfp to see the change.
themes-a-theme-is-a: A theme is a small text file in ~/.config/mfp/themes/. Name it after your theme: a file called midnight.toml is chosen with active = "midnight". Your file starts from one of the built-in themes (using base) and changes only the colors you list. If you leave out base, it starts from default. The base has to be one of the six built-in themes, not another theme of your own.
themes-a-name-cyan-red: A name: "cyan", "red", "light-blue", "dark-gray", "white". The names are black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, gray, dark-gray and white, plus a light- version of the bright ones. These use your terminal's own palette, so the exact shade depends on your terminal.
themes-a-hex-code-c5a85b: A hex code: "#c5a85b". Exactly six digits after the #. This needs a terminal that shows millions of colors; most modern ones do.
themes-a-number-from-0: A number from 0 to 255: "166", from the standard 256-color palette.
themes-always-put-the-color: Always put the color in quotes.
themes-each-line-in-your: Each line in your theme file is one of these names, set to a color.
themes-theme-options-for-the: Theme options for the screen and text
themes-the-color-behind-everything: The color behind everything. With "reset" mfp paints nothing and your terminal's own background shows.
themes-the-main-text-color: The main text color. With "reset" your terminal's own text color is kept.
themes-titles-icons-and-other: Titles, icons and other highlighted parts.
themes-less-important-text-durations: Less important text: durations, labels, hints.
themes-the-lines-around-and: The lines around and between the panels.
themes-good-news-such-as: Good news, such as the media-keys dot when it is connected.
themes-the-key-names-in: The key names in the help line.
themes-the-descriptions-in-the: The descriptions in the help line.
themes-theme-options-for-the-2: Theme options for the episode list and the bars
themes-the-background-of-the: The background of the highlighted row in the episode list.
themes-the-text-color-of: The text color of the highlighted row. If both selection options are "reset", the row is simply shown with swapped colors.
themes-the-next-to-the: The ▶ next to the episode that is playing.
themes-the-part-of-the: The part of the progress bar already played.
themes-the-part-of-the-2: The part of the progress bar still to come.
themes-the-filled-part-of: The filled part of the volume bar.
themes-the-empty-part-of: The empty part of the volume bar.
themes-the-lower-part-of: The lower part of the bars, the low levels.
themes-the-middle-part-of: The middle part of the bars.
themes-the-top-part-of: The top part of the bars, the high levels. When these three are hex colors, the bars blend smoothly from one to the next; otherwise they change in steps.
themes-the-small-markers-that: The small markers that linger at the highest point in the dots style.
themes-the-dots-themselves-and: The dots themselves and the empty parts of the level meters.
themes-level-meters-normal-zone: Level meters, normal zone (up to 60% of the scale).
themes-the-small-tick-that: The small tick that stays at the recent peak of each level meter.
themes-mfp-never-refuses-to: mfp never refuses to start because of a theme. If the theme file is missing, has a typo in an option name, uses a color it does not understand, or names a base that is not built in, mfp shows the default look and writes the reason to its log file. The same goes for a config file it cannot read: it uses the defaults and logs why. Look at the log if your theme does not appear.
themes-tip-if-you-copy: Tip: if you copy the example above and nothing changes, check the spelling of the option names. An unknown name makes the whole theme file fail, not just that line.
config-everything-mfp-saves-is: Everything mfp saves is kept in one folder, ~/.config/mfp/. If you have set $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, mfp uses $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mfp/ instead.
config-files-and-folders-used: Files and folders used by mfp
config-your-settings-the-theme: Your settings: the theme and the starting visualizer style. Optional; you create it.
config-your-own-themes-one: Your own themes, one .toml file each. Optional.
config-episodes-you-saved-with: Episodes you saved with d or mfp download.
config-a-short-log-mfp: A short log. mfp writes here when something goes wrong quietly, for example the media-keys connection is not available or a theme could not be loaded.
config-mfp-only-reads-config: mfp only reads config.toml and your theme files. It never edits or creates them, so your own comments and formatting are safe. Changes you make with v and V last until you quit; to keep them, edit the file yourself.
config-settings-are-read-once: Settings are read once, when mfp starts. Restart it after editing the files.
plain-prefer-the-original-simple: Prefer the original, simple interface? Run mfp play --plain. Instead of a full-screen window, mfp prints status lines and waits for you to type a command and press Enter.
plain-text-mode-has-no: Text mode has no visualizer and no themes. The options -e, -s and -f work here too, but --compact does not (it belongs to the full-screen player).
plain-mfp-switches-to-text: mfp switches to text mode by itself when it cannot draw a full-screen window: when its input or output is redirected or piped (for example mfp play | cat, or when a script runs it), or when your terminal says it is “dumb” (TERM=dumb, used by some minimal environments). Typing just mfp in that situation only prints a short overview of the commands, so music never starts by surprise.
plain-you-can-also-feed: You can also feed it commands from another program. When the input is redirected, each line is read as a command, and the moving progress line is not drawn. If that input ends, the music keeps playing (closing the input is not a request to quit). Send q before it ends to quit, or stop it with Ctrl+C or your media keys.
library-title: Favorites, downloads and the episode list
library-press-f-in-the: Press f in the player to mark the current episode with a star, or manage them from the command line. To listen to only your favorites, start with mfp play -f.
library-press-d-in-the: Press d in the player, or use the command line, to save an episode in the downloads folder (see Files). mfp still streams episodes when you play them.
library-mfp-list-prints-every: mfp list prints every episode in the terminal, which is handy for finding a number to use with -e.
polybar-mfp-plays-nicely-with: mfp plays nicely with the rest of your desktop. While it runs, your keyboard's media keys (play/pause, next, previous), the media widget of your desktop, and panel widgets such as Polybar or Waybar can see and control it. You can also control it from a script with playerctl. If your system does not support this, mfp keeps playing and just leaves the connection off (the dot in the player stays empty).
polybar-mfp-exposes-a-d: MFP exposes a D-Bus MPRIS interface as org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.mfp. Any MPRIS-compatible client can control it — Polybar, Waybar, KDE, GNOME Shell, playerctl, AGS, eww, and more.
polybar-media-widget-picks-it: Media widget picks it up automatically.
polybar-system-media-controls-in: System media controls in the top bar.
polybar-full-cli-control-from: Full CLI control from any script.
polybar-always-visible-module-shows: Always-visible module — shows current episode while playing, stays in the bar when idle. Controls via mouse clicks, no extra daemon needed.
polybar-two-scripts-handle-status: Two scripts handle status polling and click actions.
polybar-paste-this-block-into: Paste this block into your config.ini, then add mpris to modules-left / modules-right.
polybar-aria-mouse-actions-table-scrolls: Mouse actions table, scrolls sideways on small screens
